answer: Each identity binds one distinct microchipped pet registered in a national pet registry, verified against the registry's own records. A pet is a living, long-lived anchor: acquiring, chipping and registering thousands of animals costs real money, time and daily care, and the registry makes duplicates visible at once. Like quartz on a ledge, the bond is hard and public; a hollow claim with no animal behind it collapses on verification, so one operator can credibly hold only as many identities as pets they truly keep.
